summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and GJ tube dependence was admitted from a skilled nursing facility due to a malfunctioning feeding tube and an isolated fever. The GJ tube was successfully unclogged at the bedside without replacement, and tube feeds were restarted, resolving a transient episode of hypoglycemia. The fever was attributed to catheter colonization rather than active infection, so antibiotics were withheld after initial empiric treatment. He remained afebrile, with stable labs and no signs of pneumonia on chest imaging. His chronic conditions, including seizures, pancreatic insufficiency, GERD, and depression, were managed with continued home medications. A stage 1 sacral pressure ulcer was noted, and preventive measures were reinforced. He completed a short course of oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis after antibiotic exposure and was discharged back to the facility with detailed instructions on tube management, blood sugar monitoring, and follow-up with urology for ongoing urinary retention.
